name: appmoney
description: Estimated revenue, downloads and growth for App Store apps, and your AppMoney watchlist.

interface.longDescription:
AppMoney estimates how much apps on Apple's App Store earn and how often they are downloaded. Ask it to find apps by name, publisher, category, release date or any revenue, download, growth, rating or review range, sorted the way you need; to show the full profile of one app, with its monthly revenue and download estimates, rating, release and update dates, content rating and top countries; or to keep a watchlist of the apps you follow, filed in folders.

It is built for people who make, market, research or invest in apps and want a quick read on how an app or a category is doing.

Limitations: the figures are modelled estimates from licensed market data, not developer-reported financials, and are not financial advice. Roughly nine in ten apps have no measured figure and show only an upper bound instead of a number. Growth compares the latest two months. Apps removed from the App Store are left out unless you ask for them, and their figures stop at the last month measured. AppMoney covers the App Store only, not Google Play. Connecting needs an AppMoney account; the watchlist is the same one you see at appmoney.ai and in the AppMoney iPhone app.
capabilities: Search App Store apps by name, publisher, category or estimate range
Show one app's revenue, download, rating and release estimates
Keep a watchlist of apps, filed in folders
defaultPrompt: Which puzzle games earn the most on the App Store right now?
How much does Duolingo make a month, and how many downloads does it get?
Find finance apps whose downloads grew fastest last month.

positive.description: Rank a category by estimated revenue.
positive.prompt: Which puzzle games make the most money on the App Store right now? Show me the top 5.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_apps with the Puzzle category (7012), sorted by revenue, limit 5. Lists five puzzle games, such as Royal Match and Candy Crush Saga, each with its estimated monthly revenue and downloads, and presents the figures as estimates.

positive.description: Look up one app's full profile.
positive.prompt: How much does Duolingo earn per month, and when was it last updated?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Duolingo: Learn Languages (App Store id 570060128) and reports its estimated monthly revenue and downloads, its rating and the date of its latest update.

positive.prompt: Show me finance apps whose downloads grew more than 50% last month.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_apps with the Finance category (6015), downloads_growth_min 50 and sort install_growth. Lists matching apps with their download growth percentage and download estimates.

positive.description: Add an app to a watchlist folder.
positive.prompt: Add Headspace to my AppMoney watchlist in a folder called Wellness.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Headspace: Sleep & Meditation (App Store id 493145008), calls add_to_watchlist with folder "Wellness", and confirms Headspace is now tracked in the Wellness folder.

positive.description: Review the watchlist, then remove an app.
positive.prompt: What's on my AppMoney watchlist, and which app there earns the most? Then take Headspace off the list.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_watchlist and lists the tracked apps by folder with their estimated monthly revenue. On the test account that is Duolingo, Babbel and Busuu in Language apps, Calm unfiled, and Headspace in Wellness. It names Duolingo as the top earner, then calls remove_from_watchlist for Headspace (493145008) and confirms it is no longer tracked.

negative.description: Data AppMoney does not have: Google Play.
negative.prompt: How much does Duolingo make on Google Play?
negative.expected_behavior: Does not present an App Store figure as Google Play data. Explains that AppMoney covers Apple's App Store only, and may offer the App Store estimate instead.

negative.description: An account action the connector cannot take.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no tool. Explains that accounts cannot be deleted from the chat and points to appmoney.ai/support, where deletion is requested by email.

negative.description: A purchase, which AppMoney does not make.
negative.prompt: Buy a Calm Premium subscription for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls no tool. Explains that AppMoney only reports estimates and keeps a watchlist, and cannot buy subscriptions or make purchases.

review.commerce_description: AppMoney is free. It sells nothing, shows no plans or upgrades, and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: Resubmission of 1.0.0 after review. The privacy policy now lists every tool's inputs and outputs, what is collected, who receives it, how long it is kept and the controls users have. The website, privacy policy, terms and a new support page now name AI Humanizer, LLC as AppMoney's operator. Adds an App Store research skill that explains how to read the estimates. The MCP tools are unchanged.
